title: Source reliability
description: Whether a source is represented as reliable or unreliable from an explicit historical track record, independently of role legitimacy, current evidence quality, and testimony polarity.

contrast_conditions.label: Reliable source
contrast_conditions.definition: The same source has five historical reports in the same role and domain, with four accurate and one inaccurate report.

contrast_conditions.label: Unreliable source
contrast_conditions.definition: The same source has five historical reports in the same role and domain, with one accurate and four inaccurate reports.

probe_prompt_template:
Read the following short third-person information scenario. Track the source's historical accuracy separately from the source's role legitimacy, current evidence quality, and testimony polarity.

Scenario:
{scenario}

Continue processing the scenario.

independent_behavior_task.prompt_template: Read a separate factual question with a prior probability, a source's five-report accuracy record, and one testimony item. Report the probability that the focal claim is true from 0 to 100 as one integer. For analysis, signed testimony update is posterior minus prior for supporting testimony and prior minus posterior for contradicting testimony. Use only this item.
independence_requirements: Use new domains, source names, and claims not present in probe prompts.
Cross source track record with legitimate and non-legitimate role cues without allowing role to predict the track record.
Cross source track record with testimony polarity and current evidence quality.
Within every item, make each of the five historical reports a distinct event and claim with its own entity, setting, and time; do not repeat a report or use near-duplicate paraphrases.

The current testimony claim must be topically, event-wise, and entity-wise independent of every historical report in the same item. Do not make it a repeat, contradiction, negation, paraphrase, or year-shift variant of any historical report.
Reject any item in which the current claim reuses a historical report's entity, location, event, or date merely with a changed year or polarity; a new year alone does not make a claim independent.

Use only invented, plausible, non-retrievable source names, entities, institutions, locations, events, and dates for both historical reports and the current testimony. Do not use famous real museums, artworks, exhibitions, public figures, or recognizable world-history facts.
Do not ask the model to classify the source as reliable or unreliable.

expected_by_evidence_valence.supporting: reliable_source increases signed testimony update relative to unreliable_source
expected_by_evidence_valence.contradicting: reliable_source increases signed testimony update relative to unreliable_source

behavior.warning: This construct concerns historical track record, not authority, role legitimacy, current evidence quality, or generic social compliance.

parsing_rules.derived_outcome: signed_testimony_update = posterior - prior for supporting testimony; prior - posterior for contradicting testimony

metadata.primary_question: Does a source-track-record direction transfer to testimony weighting in a new factual domain?
